claim.why_it_matters: Markdown heading depth is flattened erratically inside the 14.8 subtree, so 14.8.2.2 renders as a peer of 14.8 rather than a child of 14.8.2, and 14.8.2.3.3 (page 601, '## 14.8.2.3.3') renders as a peer of its own grandparent. Anything that builds a TOC or outline from heading level rather than from the clause number nests these subclauses wrongly. No normative text is lost and the true depth is still recoverable from the printed clause number, which is why this is cosmetic rather than structural.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. Nothing is missing and nothing differs in content. (1) The kind label is factually wrong: all four headings are present in the transcription with the correct clause number and the correct verbatim title -- specs/ISO_COBOL.md:24966 '## 14.8.2.2 Group items', :24983 '## 14.8.2.3 Elementary items', :24986 '### 14.8.2.3.1 General', :24991 '### 14.8.2.3.2 Elementary items passed by reference'. The per-page extract E:/Temp/specrecon/v599/page-599.md lines 9, 26, 29, 34 agree, and each carries a correct anchor (section-14-8-2-2 etc.). No heading is missing, truncated, misnumbered, or mistitled. (2) The only cited difference is the number of '#' characters, which is pure markdown formatting. It carries no normative content and is explicitly within the 'difference is only formatting' rejection criterion. (3) The premise that the PDF encodes a heading depth the markdown drops is false. I looked at the rendered glyphs on spec_p599.png: '14.8.2.2 Group items', '14.8.2.3 Elementary items', '14.8.2.3.1 General' and '14.8.2.3.2 Elementary items passed by reference' are all set in the same bold serif at the same point size with the same indent. The ISO page does NOT typographically distinguish a depth-4 subclause heading from a depth-5 one. The sole depth signal the PDF carries is the dotted clause number -- and the markdown reproduces that number verbatim in every one of the four headings. The transcription therefore loses zero information the source encoded; the claim's own text concedes 'the true depth is still recoverable from the printed clause number'. (4) The finding is not a property of page 599. Across the whole transcription, 1404 of 2098 numbered headings (66.9%) have a markdown level that does not equal their clause-number depth -- e.g. '## 14.2.2 Syntax rules', '## 14.6.2.3.2 Initial state', '## 14.8.4.3 Correspondence of external data item formats'. Ad-hoc heading levels are a global convention of this OCR transcription, not a page-599 defect, so ledgering it as a page-599 discrepancy is misleading about both its location and its scale. The stated downstream consequence is also self-defeating: a TOC builder for this document cannot use heading level anyway (two thirds of the document would misnest), so it must key off the clause number, which is intact.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. All four headings on page 599 are present with correct numbers and titles; only the markdown '#' count differs from the clause-number depth. The ISO page renders depth-4 and depth-5 subclause headings in identical type, so the printed source encodes depth solely via the dotted number, which the transcription preserves verbatim -- no information is lost. Inconsistent heading levels are a document-wide property of the transcription (1404/2098 = 66.9% of numbered headings), not a page-599 defect. If the project wants clause-depth-derived heading levels, that is a one-time global normalization pass over specs/ISO_COBOL.md driven by the clause number, not a per-page reconciliation finding, and it should be tracked as a single tooling item rather than ledgered page by page.
